title: Fast Guard: Inference Sell Kit (Deck Draft)
body:
Purpose: rapid two-slide starter + technical backup for SEs to close pilots within 1–2 meetings. Not polished — intentionally lean. Use this as a swap-in for a 6‑slide live demo or a one-pager when customers ask for a 'techfriendly TL;DR'.

Slide 1 — 30s opener (customer-facing):
- Headline: Predictable LLM inference: latency you can budget for, cost you can forecast, fallbacks that keep apps live.
- 3 bullets (what matters to them): predictable p99 latency, route-level cost controls, plug-and-play private deployment option.
- Visual: tiny flow showing user -> Redwood API -> model variants (fast/cheap/accurate) -> optional private VPC.
- Speaker note: call out that model pinning + routing policy = low-risk migration path; customers can start hosted and move to Dedicated/private with same API.

Slide 2 — 60s technical reassurance (for engineers/architects):
- Headline: How we keep your app online when demand spikes or a model regresses.
- Short bullets: smart routing (latency-first / cost-first), automatic prefix/KV cache, canary + automatic fallback to compatible model variant.
- Quick checklist (for pilot kickoff): API key scoped, test prompt set uploaded, latency SLO target agreed, fallback policy chosen (auto or manual), billing threshold set.
- Speaker note: propose a 2‑week pilot: first week benchmarks + prompt-set tuning; second week soak + runbook handoff.

Slide 3 — 3x objection scripts (SE-friendly):
1) "Latency spikes":
   - Quick response: show p50/p95/p99 from our console for the route; explain autoscaling/dedicated options; offer temporary route to lower-cost, lower-latency variant.
   - Demo snippet: curl to fetch route stats (example shown live).
2) "Cost unpredictability":
   - Quick response: present token-level cost breakdown & reserve capacity options; propose caching and batching settings — suggest specific batch size delta to target 20–30% cost reduction depending on workload.
3) "Security / data residency":
   - Quick response: outline Private (VPC) path and KMS integration; offer an NDA + architecture review slot.

Slide 4 — Rapid pilot play (exact asks we want):
- 3 outcomes we measure: latency under agreed p99, per-unit cost target, no user-visible errors for 48 hours under pilot traffic.
- Required customer inputs: sample prompts (10–40), representative traffic pattern, contact for infra (SRE/NetOps).
- Our deliverables: instrumented route, baseline metrics, fallback policy config, one pager with recommended quantization/model variant.

Slide 5 — Triage flow (cheat sheet for SEs during live calls):
- If p99 > target: check concurrency + batch window, check KV cache hit rate, change routing to latency-first variant, escalate to SRE if autoscaler not spinning.
- If cost > target: enable prefix caching, switch to quantized model or lower-precision variant for non-critical requests, set cost quota alerts.
- If quality drops: rollback to pinned model version; run eval on stored prompts; open model-onboarding ticket with Applied ML.

Slide 6 — Runbook snippets and quick curl examples (to paste into demo):
- Get route stats: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/{route}/metrics
- Switch routing policy (example): curl -X PATCH ... --data '{"policy":"latency-first"}'
- Pin model version (example): curl -X POST ... --data '{"model":"redwood-v2-small@2025-02-01"}'

Unresolved / TODO (insert before finalizing deck):
- Insert up-to-date p99 numbers for common sample workloads (customer support chat, summarization at 2k tokens, embeddings batch).
- Add one short case study (internal) where fallback saved production traffic — ask SRE for incident blurb.
- Confirm exact quantization options and latency deltas for our top three model variants.

Notes to self / rough talking points (informal):
- Emphasize developer ergonomics: same API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private = low lift for platform teams.
- Keep slide deck ≤6 slides in demos — turn other material into a one-pager appendix.
- When customer says "we need on-prem": acknowledge complexity, schedule architecture deep-dive, push for pilot on Dedicated first if timeline tight.

Appendix (internal):
- Quick rebuttal lines: "If you care about cost predictability, reserved capacity + token-level dashboards are the lever — we'll help map your traffic to a reserve size."
- Slack checklist for handoff: tag #se-pilot-start, assign JIRA-INFER-1893, add pilot as label 'fast-guard'.

Why this is different: compact, multi-audience (biz + eng) two-minute opener + technical triage sheet that SEs can carry into a live call. Designed to reduce back-and-forth and get to pilot commit.

Change log: draft v0.1 — created 2025-02-11 by Aisha; 2025-03-04 Marco added triage flow edits and curl snippets.

End of draft.
